b748c1a: switchCreds returns a restore that sets fsuid, fsgid and groups back to the values read before the switch, each read back; lockAs calls it on every path and unlocks the thread only after it succeeds; an unrestorable thread stays locked, its file is closed and the joined error returned. The comment and the design note now describe the m0 park correctly. TestLockAsUsesUserCreds checks every /proc/self/task/*/status before and after 20 relocks.

e68c413 takes the suggested slots.sh fix (runuser -u "$user" -- flock -n "$f" true; posture requires runuser), so root opens no path in the user's dir. The XDG_CACHE_HOME and no-hold-through-reload residuals remain for the PR's security note.

lockas_review.restore_order: correct: fsuid first (setting it back to 0 re-raises the fs capabilities from the permitted set; CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID are never dropped by a non-zero fsuid), then fsgid, then groups, each while privileged. setfs[ug]id read back by the double call; groups by Getgroups + slices.Equal (the kernel sorts on setgroups, so the pre-switch list compares equal; empty is nil on both sides).
lockas_review.every_path: correct: restore is returned on every switchCreds failure and called unconditionally by lockAs, so a partial switch is undone; the euid==uid case and a pre-switch Getgroups failure return a no-op restore, which is right since nothing changed.
lockas_review.unlock_after_verified_restore: correct: UnlockOSThread only when restore returns nil; otherwise the fd is closed, the thread stays locked (uid/euid/suid 0) and the error propagates so quiesceSlots fails and releases its locks.
lockas_review.snapshot: correct: prior fsuid/fsgid taken as os.Geteuid()/os.Getegid(), valid since nothing else in warden changes fs ids; prior groups read on the locked thread.
lockas_review.test: adequate: allTasksRoot requires Uid/Gid '0 0 0 0' and root's groups on every task and skips exiting tasks. Nit, not a finding: relock's comment ('A thread a call leaves locked is replaced') describes the pre-fix behaviour; the 20 calls remain a sound regression check.

slots_sh_review: runuser -u opens the lock as the owner with initgroups, mirroring lockAs. flock(1) opens with O_CREAT, but as the user and after [ -f ], so harmless. Any non-zero exit (held, permission, runuser failure) counts as busy, which fails safe. No guide lists slots.sh's required tools, so the posture change leaves no reference doc stale (UX-01). An owner-planted FIFO still blocks the script, now in the user's flock child (finding 16).

findings.finding: New in b748c1a. restore's group read-back formats err with %v: fmt.Errorf("restoring groups: got %v (%v), want %v", got, err, groups). tier1's errorlint check (GLOBAL-03 error-wrap) flags it under GOOS=linux only, since the file is _linux; the commit's FLOW-17 per-platform lint was missed.
findings.suggestion: Split the cases rather than using %w (which would print %!w(<nil>) on a mismatch): got, err := unix.Getgroups(); if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("reading groups back: %w", err) }; if !slices.Equal(got, groups) { return fmt.Errorf("restoring groups: got %v, want %v", got, groups) }. Re-run GOOS=linux make lint.
